Rolle's theorem deals with the graph of a function that crosses the x-axis at two different points, f(a) and f(b). Rolle's Theorem If y = f(x) is continuous at every point of the closed interval [a,b] and differentiable at every point of its interior (a,b) and f(a) = f(b) = 0, then there is at least one number c between a and b where f'(c) = 0.Q

SLOPES AND TANGENT LINES - The first derivative of a function gives the slope of the tangent line at any point on the graph of the function. A horizontal line has a slope of zero so the point where f'(x) = 0 indicates that there is a horizontal tangent line at this point. The slope of the tangent line is negative when the function decreases (falls) and positive when the function increases (rises).
